Cuphead is mostly a hardcore boss rush game with some platforming levels in between, which reminds me of Contra. Co-op would typically make the game feel even harder because of how chaotic it could get. The art style is amazing and is a big selling point of the game. It feels like Disney pictures from the old days.

However, the difficulty is too high for my liking and the film grain effects cannot be turned off. Fortunately, mods that provide assist modes and accessibility options can be found online, which make the gameplay experience much better.

This game is fun to play and the art style is really unique. However, it's also very challenging. My best advice is playing attention to boss patterns so you can learn and anticipate. Highly recommend watching youtube videos if you struggle as well.

Great game, great soundtrack, amazing visuals, ran well, didn't find any bugs, you can feel the love and hard work put into it, recommend checking the making of this game if you enjoy this sort of thing

I’m not sure about keyboard controls as I played with a controller. Controller for the most part is easy to use.

9/10, some DLC would be neat.

Time to delve into expert mode yew.

Cuphead has nearly everything going for it. Hand-drawn, amazing art. Music reminiscent of a time long past. Memorable bosses. It's got it all, right?

Nah. The game-play sucks.

The controls must have been designed by a monkey. There's no excuse for how bad these controls are, ESPECIALLY for the keyboard. Why not integrate the mouse? Why force players to have to hold down the shoot button until their fingers pop off? Why attach aiming to movement? It's baffling.

I've beaten every level up to the dragon boss, and I just stopped there. Not because I didn't think I could beat the game, but because I just didn't want to. It's a game that's hard because its controls are frustrating, not because the game-play is truly challenging.

I hope you have patience, because this game is nothing but that.
almost everything in this game is a boss. each boss, of course, has a select amount of different attacks that must be learned and mastered while stuff in the background will attack at the same time. I had a way worse time with the run and gun levels (move from one side of a really long horizontal level to the other while enemies are placed strategically to make players the most mad), taking up to two hours to get one completed. how did it take so long? well, I am a perfectionist, so I was going for P (pacifist) rank on every single one. I have many memories of sweating, yelling, even getting headaches over this game, but I'm glad I played it. my skill has improved significantly, and I can go through the whole game without dying to at least 50% of the bosses.
TL;DR: do not play this game unless you have a lot of patience and inner peace (unless you dont mind getting angry), but the game is fun once you get good at it.
(I was NOT a huge fan of the dlc bosses though)

Cuphead is one of the best and most polished games I have ever had the pleasure of playing. From the gameplay and boss design to the art direction and music, everything has been given so much love, care and talent into it it makes hard not to want to play it until your eyes fall out or turn square. Highly recommend this one, it is, for me, one of the only 10/10 games out there. (everything i said also applies to the DLC, that in my opinion is a must have as well)

Much has been made of the difficulty. It is hard, and I thought the final boss was a little unfair at times, but in general it is very manageable for any veteran of platformers and it manages to keep you involved via the amazing visuals while you die repeatedly. There is also an easier difficulty level you can switch to, although I think you must beat all the earlier stages on the standard difficulty to unlock the final stage.

On a sidenote, I'm not sure if this was a ripoff or an homage, but I adored the callback to my favorite Gunstar Heroes level, the Dice Palace.

Just a pure masterpiece of a game, beautifully handcrafted and extremely fun. Difficulty is just for me, keep trying and you'll get it eventually. But there are a couple of bugs regarding hitboxes, which are rather quite rare. Local Co-Op is fucking awesome and I love that this game proved that you don't have to have online play to be successful. Although online co-op would be great, I understand the devs didn't have enough resource to implement that (after all, they had to mortgage their house to finish the game!), and it doesn't matter because new DLC has been confirmed and will come out very soon. 10/10.

This game is amazing. The 1930's animation and music are some of the most original ideas I've ever seen in gaming. The gameplay is difficult, but it feels so rewarding to finish a boss especially the really hard ones. (For me Dr. Kahl's Robot took a week to beat.) And the Soundtrack is so good, considering Kristofer Maddigan had no experience with big band or jazz before. The animation is incredible and each boss seems unique and creative in it's own way, though I have to say the bosses are definitely the highlight while the Run n' Gun's seem worse and eluding to be a change of pace, but I can't complain because those levels are really creative as well. 10/10

Cuphead

Cuphead is a 2D shooter with the artstyle of the 1930s. I think the game is good, but it's nothing to write home about. It's very fun, but lacks replayablity unless you go for 100%.

The visuals and the artstyle is alright. They definitely nailed what they were going for, though I don't think the artstyle look "good" persay. The reason I say this is because the artstyle is perfect for what it's trying to be, but just because it looks like what its trying to be, doesn't mean it looks good. I mean if someone were to make a game that tried to look like the mod "The Binning of Isek" nobody would think it looks good, because the artstyle is bad, and that's kind what i'm trying to say for Cuphead. It's not bad, but it's not good either.

The difficulty is ok, it's difficult at times and if your a casual to hardcore-gamer you're going to die a bunch in this game.

I think I would give it more of a "meh" score if given the option, but as it stands I think it's a solid game.

I give this game a 2.5/5, it's solid but I guess it's not the game for me.

I appreciate the effort, I really do. The animation is gorgeous, the soundtrack is snazzy and jazzy, the storyline and the characters are fun, and I bet the game is offering an expert challenge for the veterans of the platforming genre.

Here's the catch, it's the Dark Souls of platformers.

If someone would finish this game 100%, they'd be qualified to do the speedruns of it. But maybe it's your thing. If you want a tough-as-nails challenge, this is your game. Me? I'll continue to enjoy the soundtrack, and watch the Let's Play videos of the game whenever I want to reminisce it.

Cuphead "Don't Deal With the Devil" is one of the most imaginative and beautiful game i've ever played. The bosses are all unique and diverse. The game's difficulty is where it really shines, some people could have shrugged it of as "Non difficult" or "Easy" but under the game's cartoony fascade hides a rage enducing run-and-gun platformer in the vain of games similar to Contra. This game was an enjoyable experience and I loved every minute of it. Can't wait for the DLC.
